We ignore side effects of functions, meaning function calls do not modify their arguments.

The value of `in` is independent of `name`. The condition at line 14 checks `name.indexOf('\\') != -1`, which leads to the block containing line 27, but that condition only controls whether line 27 is executed, not the value of `in`. The value of `in` itself is not derived from `name`. So the value of `in` before line 27 does not depend on the value of `name` after line 2.

Thus answer is No.
